legacy_metadata.method: run.sh.txt ran HermiT once on each input. Its comparison step passed ELK's taxonomy to el-oracle.py in the wrong form, so oracle.sh.txt made the retained comparisons again from the same taxonomies without running HermiT: scripts/el-oracle.py HERMIT.ofn OURS.txt against the classifier, and ref-compare.py.txt HERMIT.ofn ELK.ofn, which reads two reference files with el-oracle's own reader and counts the classes either side names alone. compare.jsonl holds both reports, hermit.jsonl HermiT's JSON lines and cases/ the four test ontologies with each tool's taxonomy. HermiT ran on one thread; the threads field of hermit.jsonl gives the unused --threads default of that harness version.

legacy_metadata.method: run.sh.txt ran each reasoner once per input and compared its taxonomy with the classifier's (gen-ours.sh.txt wrote those) and, for the range cases, with HermiT's, through scripts/el-oracle.py. The first range and big pass of Whelk failed in the harness, which commit 91a7b160 fixed, and the batch then ran Whelk again with ONLY=whelk, so env.txt lists three starts. The robot stage timed each ROBOT command with timed.py.txt from the release's RDF/XML file, or from the functional-style file for the -ofn rows, to the written functional-style output, and checked each output's asserted named hierarchy with el-oracle.py --asserted against the classifier's taxonomy. The batch's sparkles runs failed because the release binary had been removed from the build directory, so the four sparkles-classify rows of robot/runs.jsonl after the failed ones ran afterwards with the same binary under the same cap. closure.py.txt counts the subsumptions between named classes that two taxonomies entail, with each class's equivalent classes and the classes above its node, after el-oracle.py's normalization. The Whelk package of these runs is the build of commit 91a7b160 that env.txt names. Commit ea96e8f5 later made the harness treat an unsatisfiable owl:Thing as inconsistent, which changes none of these results, since Whelk reported the inconsistent ontologies here as inconsistent itself.
